findings.evidence: Preface cross-reference rule (PDF p.23): 'Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N.' Body uses four different section forms: PDF p.3 'Appendix A §10'; PDF p.74 'accessed 2026-08-30; A.10'; PDF p.100 'Appendix A's §A.7 (Fig A.2, vendor-relative KV/compute ratios)'; PDF p.63 'Appendix A §9A'. List of Figures (PDF p.9): 'A.3 A chronology of frontier AI systems, ~2017 to ~2026 ... 492'. Preface (PDF p.17): 'a superseding re-verification of the DeepSeek model-service status (Appendix A, A.3)'; also (PDF p.22) 'the dated note itself at Appendix A, A.6 or A.3'.
findings.issue: Malformed and colliding Appendix A cross-references. (a) The stated convention requires a letter suffix on section labels ('§ 9A'), but the body writes '§10', 'A.10', '§A.7' and '§9A' — four incompatible forms for section references. (b) 'A.3' resolves to two different targets: List of Figures assigns A.3 to the chronology figure (printed p.492) while the Preface uses 'Appendix A, A.3' for a DeepSeek model-service status text note; the same collision exists for 'A.6' (Preface text note vs. figure numbering) even though List of Figures stops at A.5.
findings.fix_instruction: Adopt one section form everywhere (e.g. 'Appendix A § 10A' style matching the stated 'letter suffix' rule) and convert every body instance ('Appendix A §10' p.3, 'A.10' p.74, '§A.7' p.100) to it; reserve bare 'A.N' for figures only, and rewrite the Preface's 'Appendix A, A.3' / 'A.6' / 'A.10' text-note references (PDF pp.17, 22) to the section form so they stop colliding with figure A.3 (PDF p.9).

findings.evidence: Page 33 (§1.3): "If average request is ~9.2K input + ~300 output ≈ 9.5K tokens per request, and traffic is ~10 req/s, then the system ingests: • Input tokens/s: 9,200 tokens/req × 10 req/s = 92,000 tokens/s (peaks higher at ~40 req/s → ~368k). • Output tokens/s: 300 ×10 = 3,000 tokens/s output. • Roughly 30× more input tokens than output tokens in this workload (9,200 ÷ 300 ≈ 30.7, carried book-wide as the canonical ~30×, Ch. 4, Table 4-2)."
findings.issue: The 30× input/output ratio is presented in Ch. 1 as the canonical book-wide constant and is explicitly tied to Ch. 4 Table 4-2, but Table 4-2 (p. 76–79, the canonical-scenario provenance ledger that the book designates as the single authority for canonical values) contains no input/output ratio row — it lists input tokens 9,200 and output tokens 300 separately and never states a 30× ratio. The same chapter-1 text calls Table 1-1 (p. 36) "Token throughput of the canonical workload", but the ratio row in that table is itself labeled "canonical scenario [DERIVED]" with the derivation "9,200 ÷ 300 ≈ 30.7, rounded down to the canonical ~30× for convenience (not to the nearest integer, 31)". So the ratio's authoritative home (Table 1-1) contradicts the cross-reference Ch. 1 makes to Table 4-2.
findings.fix_instruction: Either add an explicit input/output ratio row to Table 4-2 (Ch. 4, p. 76–79) with its [canonical scenario][DERIVED] status, or correct the Ch. 1 citations from "Ch. 4, Table 4-2" to "Table 1-1" so the ratio's provenance points at the table that actually records it.

findings.evidence: Page 37 (§1.5 Common Mistakes): "• Ignoring the input/output asymmetry. Treating a request as 'one unit' hides that input-heavy workloads tend toward high prefill compute and KV-capacity pressure, while output-heavy ones are decode-dominant (run-time per generated token) — opposite bottlenecks with opposite fixes. (Note: 'capacity pressure' is a memory-capacity constraint, not a memory-bandwidth bound; see Ch. 4/8.)"
findings.issue: The cross-reference "see Ch. 4/8" is not a resolvable reference under the book's own convention. The Preface (p. xix) defines the reference form: "A section reference takes the form § N.M ... so § 7.3 and § 7.3 name the same reference" and "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." "Ch. 4/8" names two chapters joined by a slash with no section anchor and no target topic — it does not resolve to a specific discussion, and Ch. 4's Chapter-Question scope (workload characterization) does not contain a capacity-vs-bandwidth distinction, while Ch. 8 (Compute) and Ch. 7 (Memory) do. The note's own content — that KV pressure is a capacity constraint rather than a bandwidth bound — is stated in Ch. 7 §7.3 (p. 143, the concurrency ceiling) and Ch. 8 (roofline), but Ch. 4 does not carry it as its defining content.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace "see Ch. 4/8" with resolvable anchors that actually state the capacity-vs-bandwidth distinction, e.g. "see § 7.3 (concurrency ceiling) and § 8.2 (roofline ridge)", so the reference follows the book's § N.M convention and points at sections that discuss the cited point.

findings.evidence: Page 33 (§1.3): "• Input tokens/s: 9,200 tokens/req × 10 req/s = 92,000 tokens/s (peaks higher at ~40 req/s → ~368k)." and "• Output tokens/s: 300 ×10 = 3,000 tokens/s output."
findings.issue: The peak output rate is not stated in this worked example even though the peak input rate is (368k), and the same peak/avg asymmetry recurs as a bare, unlabeled number: the parenthesis gives "~368k" with no unit (tokens/s) while the surrounding lines use full units. The reader must infer that ~368k is tokens/s input; the corresponding output figure (300 × 40 = 12,000 tok/s) is absent, so the two legs of the peak rate are not paired. Later chapters do print the pair (p. 70: "~368,000 tokens/s ... and ~12,000 respectively"; p. 83), so Ch. 1's treatment is the outlier.
findings.fix_instruction: Add the peak output rate to the Ch. 1 worked example (300 × 40 = 12,000 output tok/s) and give the ~368k figure its unit (input tokens/s), so both legs of the peak rate are stated with units as they are in Ch. 4.
